review.reason: Candidate 24 passes as supplied. Hole 1 is a dry 578-yard par 5 with a clear staged route and multiple fairway bunkers; reaching the green in three is supported by the simulation, while only 3 of 9 tee-dispersion samples finish safely in short grass, adding challenge without eliminating playable outcomes. Hole 2 is a 184-yard island-green par 3 with a substantial surrounding lake and a 3-wood tee shot. Its target carry contrasts sharply with the opener, and the dispersion probes indicate it remains playable. Hole 3 is a 426-yard split-fairway par 4 with water to the right and forward of the green. Its broad landing area leaves room to choose a safer line or challenge the hazard for position. The par-5/3/4 sequence, varied tee clubs, and changing hazard and landing-zone demands create strong internal variety. Recent rounds have included island targets and long par 5s, so the combination is not wholly novel, but the dry staged opener and water-influenced split-fairway finish distinguish it sufficiently. The simulations and dispersion results support a challenging, recoverable round rather than three routine holes.
